items.text: Combine the aqueous solution of 0.21 g hydrated M(II) nitrate (either Cu or Ni) with 25 mL CHCl3 and 0.18 g sodium octanoate; stir vigorously. Discard the clear aqueous phase and retain the colored organic phase. The source describes this common precursor-preparation sequence for the NiS and Cu2S comparators. Add 240 μL dodecanethiol, stir vigorously 30 min, then evaporate the organic solvent on a rotary evaporator to leave a waxy metal-thiolate/octanoate mixture. Heat the waxy precursor mixture in air. The article gives broad temperature and duration ranges shared across preparations, without linking a specific thermolysis setting to each Figure 8 specimen. Product color is reported as dark brown or black depending on heating time and temperature. Disperse in chloroform, precipitate with excess ethanol, centrifuge; discard the supernatant containing unreacted precursors and byproducts. After ethanol precipitation, redisperse in chloroform and centrifuge; discard the precipitate to remove insoluble byproducts and poorly passivated particles. Retain the chloroform-dispersed product. TEM samples were drop-cast from either hexane, toluene, or chloroform dispersions onto 200-mesh carbon-coated copper grids (Ladd Research); the paper does not map a solvent to every figure. Low- to intermediate-resolution TEM images were acquired with a Philips 208 TEM at 80 kV using an AMT Advantage HR model CCD camera.
